name: 1900 Prairie Avenue (the Elbridge G. Keith house): the brick stable on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Robinson's 1886 plate 10, which dates the 1600 and 1700 blocks' stables, stops at 18th Street, and nothing else read dates this one, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 28 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_28.jpg) at pixel (566.67, 3777.54): the alley wall's line, read by median darkness profile at rows 3680-3720, 3740-3780, 3840-3880 and 3900-3940 (567.44, 566.83, 566.39, 565.67; the raster leans about 0.6 degrees, so the line is fitted through the four), halfway between the building's north and south wall lines (3625.03 and 3930.05). Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json): local E 1339.397, N -3348.735, 0.23 m north of the middle of parcel prairie_1900's rear line, plus the datum origin. The bearing is the parcel's own (its north and south lines run at 0.616 degrees north of east), so the building's ends lie along the lot lines.
placement.symbolic_location: 1900 S. Prairie Avenue: west side of Prairie between 18th and 20th Streets, parcel prairie_1900 (data/street_grid/1904.json), the lot south of the strip between 1834 and 1900; on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the east line of the alley between Indiana and Prairie.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 566.67 at its middle row; the line read by median darkness profile at rows 3680-3720, 3740-3780, 3840-3880 and 3900-3940 as 567.44, 566.83, 566.39 and 565.67, the raster leaning about 0.6 degrees) to its east wall line (748.80, 748.01, 746.97 and 746.29 at the same rows; 747.66 at the middle row), 180.98 pixels at the sheet's 0.050558 m a pixel, 9.15 m deep, and from its north wall line (row 3625.03, the line it shares with the frame shed on the strip between 1834 and 1900, which the sheet draws once) to its south one (3930.05, the line it shares with 1906's building), 305.01 pixels, 15.42 m along the alley. It is one rectangle: no piece, wing or open strip. The kit's party walls stand inside this outline at both ends, their returns 0.5 m past the eaves, which is the kit's and not the sheet's; the shed and 1906's building are still the district draft's.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the building's north-west corner, just south of its north wall line (the '1' just north of that line is the frame shed's; the T-1841 census row read the building as '1-storey', which the sheet does not bear out). Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under the kit's 40-degree roof (3.84 m from eave to ridge over the 9.15 m span); those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick. The '12 8' written across its south wall line stands on the line it shares with 1906's building and is read as the two walls' thicknesses in inches, the sheet's practice at 1834's north wall; the kit builds its own 13-inch walls.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick, the fire-wall sign and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1900-stable-1935. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, the key's fire-wall sign with two ticks at the alley end of its north wall line, and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, a cross with a dot for each storey (the sign 1816's, 1824's and 1834's alley walls carry), 7.86 m from the north wall line (row 3780.5) and 7.56 m from the south. It letters the building GARAGE, a 1911 use not carried to 1904. Both ends are party walls: the north on the fire-wall sign, against the frame shed on the strip between 1834 and 1900; the south on the line the sheet draws once with 1906's two-storey building (as 1834's north wall stands on the line it shares with 1828's), so there is no open gable. The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s counts from the north party wall's inner face, 0.33 m in, on the alley wall, and from the south party wall's inner face on the yard wall). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for 15.4 m: two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard where the walk to the house meets it and four stable sash with loft sash over them. The kit's 40-degree gable runs its ridge along the alley, 3.84 m from eave to ridge over the 9.15 m span, with no dormer. The workyard is paved from the yard door 14.04 m east to the west face of the house's one-storey frame rear porch (sheet column 1025.4, rows 3696.6-3844.6), the walk on that porch's middle, 0.35 m north of the building's. A small ring the sheet draws inside the building's south-west corner (about column 585, row 3915), as it does inside 1824's, is not read and builds nothing.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof, party walls and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED except where the window mark places a sash. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 28 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 1900, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is a 1911 use and is not read as the 1904 one (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1841 census row s28-1900-rear: 'its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house'). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house, as 1726's GARAGE is (T-1932): two carriage bays, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source read names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-1935 refines the district draft (T-2329) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the fourth of the package's seven alley buildings on the west side of Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th, after 1816's, 1824's and 1834's. The sheet census (census row s28-1900-rear, trace s28fp-1900-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 28 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangle: the sheet draws a building 9.15 m deep and 15.42 m along the alley on the alley line, filling the lot's width, its north wall on the line it shares with the one-storey frame shed on the strip between 1834 and 1900 (where the key's fire-wall sign stands at the alley end) and its south wall on the line it shares with 1906's two-storey building. The census row reads the building as '1-storey'; the sheet letters '2' in its north-west corner (the '1' just north of the line is the frame shed's), so this record builds two storeys and the draft's one-storey body is retired. Robinson's 1886 atlas (plate 10) stops at 18th Street, so nothing read here dates the building before 1911. The one picture the T-1935 image gate names for it (Clark's c. 1905 street view north from 1936) shows the house fronts on Prairie Avenue and not the alley.
